domain.name: Unity Production
domain.description: Advanced Unity production covering scalable architecture, editor tooling, managed content loading, animation systems, shaders, performance, memory, and build diagnostics. Version-sensitive APIs and package behavior belong in Current Intelligence.

competencies.name: Scalable Gameplay Architecture
competencies.description: Structure gameplay systems around explicit state, services, events, data ownership, and testable boundaries.
competencies.purpose: Keep larger Unity projects maintainable as features multiply.

units.title: Architecture is dependency control
units.content: Good Unity architecture makes ownership, lifetime, dependencies, and communication explicit instead of hiding them in scene searches or global state.

units.title: System decomposition workflow
units.content: Define responsibilities and lifetimes, separate data from presentation, make dependencies explicit, isolate engine-facing adapters, design events narrowly, and test scene reload and failure behavior.

units.title: Architecture failure modes
units.content: Avoid god managers, circular service dependencies, hidden static state, scene-wide searches as dependency injection, and scripts that mix input, rules, persistence, and UI.

drills.title: Design a scalable interaction architecture
drills.prompt: Design Unity systems for player state, interactions, inventory, save data, and UI without one central god object.

competencies.name: Editor Tooling & Serialization
competencies.description: Build custom inspectors, validation, asset processors, editor utilities, and serialization-safe workflows.
competencies.purpose: Move repeatable production checks into tools without corrupting serialized project data.

units.title: Editor automation touches persistent project state
units.content: Custom editor code can modify assets, prefabs, scenes, import settings, and serialized data; tools need explicit scope and undo or rollback behavior.

units.title: Editor-tool workflow
units.content: Define a narrow task, inspect serialized targets, support preview or validation first, integrate Undo where appropriate, batch deterministically, log changes, and verify source-control diff after execution.

units.title: Editor-tool failures
units.content: Avoid mutating assets during simple inspection, changing many project files with no report, depending on current selection silently, and bypassing serialization APIs with uncontrolled text edits.

drills.title: Build an editor asset validator
drills.prompt: Design a Unity editor tool that checks textures, meshes, prefabs, naming, and import settings before build.

competencies.name: Advanced Content Loading & Addressables
competencies.description: Design memory-aware content groups, runtime references, caching, update paths, and unload behavior.
competencies.purpose: Scale content without loading the whole project or leaking memory.

units.title: A runtime reference can keep an asset alive
units.content: Memory release depends on reference ownership and load/unload lifecycles, not only whether a scene was closed.

units.title: Managed-content workflow
units.content: Group content by lifetime and update strategy, define ownership of handles, test cold and warm loads, measure memory before and after unload, verify failure paths, and version remote-content assumptions separately.

units.title: Content-loading failures
units.content: Avoid duplicate loads with unclear owners, never-released handles, giant groups that defeat streaming, synchronous loads in critical frames, and changing group strategy without rebuild validation.

drills.title: Design streamed neighborhood content
drills.prompt: Plan loading groups and lifetimes for a city environment with buildings, interiors, audio, traffic, and UI.

competencies.name: Advanced Animation Systems & Playables
competencies.description: Coordinate Animator layers, masks, procedural control, timelines, Playables, and runtime blending.
competencies.purpose: Handle complex character and cinematic motion without brittle transition webs.

units.title: Animation control can be layered by responsibility
units.content: Locomotion, upper-body actions, procedural offsets, cinematics, and facial motion often need distinct ownership and blending policies.

units.title: Animation-system workflow
units.content: Define movement ownership, state and parameter contracts, layer masks, interruption rules, root motion policy, and cinematic overrides; profile transitions and test recovery from interrupted states.

units.title: Animation-system failures
units.content: Avoid overlapping systems writing the same transform, parameter sprawl with unclear semantics, unbounded transition conditions, and cinematic control that cannot hand state back cleanly.

drills.title: Design a layered character animation stack
drills.prompt: Plan locomotion, aim, interaction, hit reactions, and cutscene control for one character.

competencies.name: Shader Graph & Render Features
competencies.description: Build reusable shader systems and custom rendering features while respecting platform cost.
competencies.purpose: Achieve advanced visuals without losing performance accountability.

units.title: Shader complexity multiplies across pixels and objects
units.content: A visually small graph can be expensive when used on large screen coverage, transparency, many lights, or many objects.

units.title: Shader-development workflow
units.content: Define visual requirement, establish cheapest baseline, modularize shared functions, expose bounded parameters, inspect generated cost where possible, profile representative scenes, and provide lower-cost variants when needed.

units.title: Shader failure modes
units.content: Avoid expensive branches by default, uncontrolled transparency, texture-sample growth, solving all effects in one mega-shader, and judging cost only in editor preview.

drills.title: Build and profile a stylized surface shader
drills.prompt: Design a reusable urban surface shader with masks, wetness, emission, and distance-aware cost control.

competencies.name: Parallel Jobs, Burst & Data-Oriented Work
competencies.description: Recognize workloads suitable for parallel jobs and data-oriented processing without premature complexity.
competencies.purpose: Accelerate CPU-heavy systems only when profiling supports it.

units.title: Parallelism rewards simple data flow
units.content: Large independent workloads become easier to parallelize when data is contiguous, ownership is clear, and side effects are minimized.

units.title: Parallelization decision workflow
units.content: Profile a CPU bottleneck, isolate pure or batchable work, define data layout, remove shared mutation, prototype a job-based version, compare overhead and correctness, then keep it only if the measured gain matters.

units.title: Parallelism failure modes
units.content: Avoid moving tiny workloads into jobs, unsafe shared state, synchronization that erases gains, and adopting package-specific patterns without verifying the current Unity version.

drills.title: Evaluate a crowd workload for parallelization
drills.prompt: Decide which parts of a large NPC update loop should remain main-thread and which could move to jobs.

competencies.name: Memory, GC & Runtime Performance
competencies.description: Diagnose allocations, object churn, pooling, memory growth, frame spikes, and managed/native cost.
competencies.purpose: Stabilize frame time and memory under real gameplay load.

units.title: Average frame rate can hide damaging spikes
units.content: User experience depends on frame-time distribution, allocation patterns, loading stalls, and memory pressure, not only average FPS.

units.title: Performance investigation loop
units.content: Capture representative build data, identify CPU/GPU/memory category, inspect allocations and spikes, isolate one hot path, change one cause, compare traces, and repeat until within target.

units.title: Performance failure modes
units.content: Avoid pooling everything by reflex, optimizing editor-only costs, removing allocations without measuring frame impact, and trading stable memory for uncontrolled caches.

drills.title: Diagnose periodic GC spikes
drills.prompt: Create a measurement-first plan for recurring stutters during active gameplay.

competencies.name: Build Pipeline & Platform Debugging
competencies.description: Operate repeatable build configuration, CI-friendly builds, platform differences, logs, symbols, and runtime diagnostics.
competencies.purpose: Turn editor success into reproducible target-platform delivery.

units.title: The build environment is part of the product
units.content: Editor version, packages, project settings, scripting backend, build target, defines, assets, and environment variables all affect output reproducibility.

units.title: Build failure isolation
units.content: Capture exact environment and error, reproduce from a clean state, separate compile from packaging from runtime failure, inspect player logs, compare target-specific settings, and preserve the last known-good artifact.

units.title: Build pipeline failures
units.content: Avoid changing packages during a release emergency, debugging runtime crashes only from editor behavior, ignoring platform case sensitivity or permissions, and overwriting the known-good build.

drills.title: Diagnose a target-only build failure
drills.prompt: Plan isolation for a Unity project that works in editor but fails on the target device.
